name: CDM collateral prototype
description: Local prototype architecture for CDM-based initial-margin management with tokenized collateral on Hyperledger Besu.

nodes.name: Participant stack
nodes.description: Per-participant deployment (ADR wp-adr-per-participant-services): each simulated participant runs its own party console, collateral workflow service, workflow store, ledger gateway and keystore, holding only its own books and its own signing key, and connected to its own Besu validator node. N stacks run side by side; the oracle service, mock market data and contracts are shared.

metadata.instances: N, one per participant (pledgor, secured party, market operator)
metadata.isolation: own process, own SQLite file, own key; no shared database

nodes.name: CDM collateral prototype
nodes.description: Prototype that illustrates CDM-based initial-margin management with tokenized collateral segregated by a smart contract on a local Besu network. Nothing is deployed outside the developer machine.

nodes.name: Collateral workflow service
nodes.description: Off-chain margin workflow (ASR concept-asr-onchain-call-state: negotiation and CDM content off-chain, call state on-chain), one instance per participant: holds that party's CDM agreements (ISDA IM CSA / CTA-SA elections, eligibility schedule), checks eligibility and haircuts with CDM functions, runs the margin call lifecycle (issue, respond, dispute, propose, decide, settle) that CDM 7.7.0 does not provide (finding F2) with the local CDM extension (cdm-ext), and sends its own party's movement instructions to its ledger gateway. Each lifecycle step is one CDM MarginCallInstruction serialised to canonical Rune JSON and hashed with keccak-256; the service writes the document to the CDM payload store and the hash goes on-chain (ADR wp-adr-cdm-payload-carrier). It reads the counterparty's steps from the chain and the store, not from the counterparty's instance, and folds every step in chain order into one cumulative, validated MarginCallState per call (CDM Create_MarginCallState); both parties' folds converge to an identical state. It relays its gateway's event stream to its console over Server-Sent Events.

metadata.cdm-binding: CDM 7.7.0 Java (org.finos.cdm:cdm-java) and the local extension cdmx generated to Java (cdm-ext), ADR wp-adr-java-cdm-stack

nodes.name: CDM 7.7.0 object model
nodes.description: FINOS Common Domain Model release 7.7.0 (commit 1c97666, Java distribution) as the canonical data layer (ASR concept-asr-cdm-data-layer): LegalAgreement with CSA IM / CTA elections, EligibleCollateralSpecification, MarginCallIssuance / MarginCallResponse, CollateralPortfolio. Extended locally (cdm-ext, namespaces cdmx.*: margin call lifecycle, events, transfers) and with on-chain asset identity (ASR concept-asr-onchain-asset-identity, finding B1).

nodes.name: Workflow store
nodes.description: One SQLite file per participant holding that party's agreements, margin calls and responses, disputes, movement instructions, collateral balances and the asset registry that maps ISIN/CUSIP and DTI to network and token contract.

nodes.name: CDM payload store
nodes.description: Content-addressed store for the CDM document of every margin call lifecycle step (ADR wp-adr-cdm-payload-carrier). A document is stored under its keccak-256 hash, which is also the cdmHash the margin call contract records for that step: the hash is the retrieval key and the integrity check (the store rejects a body that does not hash to its key, and a reader recomputes the hash). Each document carries a reader allowlist of the call's two counterparty addresses. Callers authenticate with a per-party bearer token that the store resolves to the party's address; it fails closed with no tokens configured. One shared instance serves all participants.

metadata.authentication: per-party bearer token (shared secret, PARTY_TOKENS / STORE_TOKEN)
metadata.production: mutual TLS or signed requests; a shared content-addressed store or IPFS with access control, or per-party stores

nodes.name: Oracle service
nodes.description: Off-chain oracle endpoints, shared, run by the market data operator. Reads price / NAV and rating data from the mock market data source, serves it to every participant's collateral service for valuation and eligibility, and publishes signed updates on-chain through the operator's ledger gateway. Also relays a default notice from the secured party to the on-chain default feed.

nodes.name: Mock market data source
nodes.description: Local JSON files standing in for NAV, price and rating providers (in the GDF/ISDA sandbox: Kaiko, Redstone, Moody's).

nodes.name: Ledger gateway
nodes.description: Ledger-neutral interface (ASR concept-asr-ledger-neutrality, ADR wp-adr-prototype-ledgers): one instance per participant: accepts its participant's movement instructions (and, for the operator, oracle updates), signs with that participant's key only and submits transactions to the ledger, waits for finality, serves a call's lifecycle steps in chain order with their cdmHash, and pushes chain events to the collateral service over Server-Sent Events from one eth_subscribe subscription on its Besu node. Besu adapter first; a Canton adapter is the second target.

nodes.name: Development keystore
nodes.description: Per participant: the private key of that participant's test account only (pledgor, secured party, or for the market operator the oracle publisher and contract admin keys). Development keys only.

nodes.name: Besu local network
nodes.description: Hyperledger Besu network in Docker Compose with QBFT consensus: four validator nodes, one per default participant (market operator, BANK-A, BANK-B, BANK-C), each participant's gateway connected to its own node (ADR wp-adr-per-participant-services). Deterministic finality per block (ASR concept-asr-settlement-finality); blocks continue with one node down. Stands in for a permissioned network such as DTCC's private Besu network.

metadata.consensus: QBFT, four validators, one node per participant

nodes.name: Tokenized collateral contracts
nodes.description: ERC-20 test tokens with transfer restrictions standing in for a tokenized money market fund and a tokenized US Treasury. Each token records its ISIN/CUSIP and DTI as metadata (ASR concept-asr-onchain-asset-identity).

nodes.name: Collateral control contract
nodes.description: Smart contract that holds pledged initial margin (ADR wp-adr-im-segregation). States per pledge: pledged, returned, enforced. Pledge: pledgor transfers tokens in, only against an agreed call whose collateral proposal the secured party accepted, only the accepted assets, and up to the agreed amount; the call is then marked settled. Return: needs approval by both parties or by the secured party. Enforce: secured party only, after the default feed reports a default. No other movement is possible.

nodes.name: Margin call contract
nodes.description: Records each margin call on-chain (ASR concept-asr-onchain-call-state, ADR wp-adr-margin-call-state-onchain): ID, agreement, caller and called party, called, agreed and disputed amounts, settlement deadline, call state (issued, agreed, partially agreed, disputed, settled), collateral proposal state (proposed, accepted, rejected) with the proposed assets and quantities, and for every lifecycle step the keccak-256 cdmHash of its CDM document, emitted on the step's event (CallIssued, CallAnswered, CollateralProposed, ProposalDecided, CallSettled; ADR wp-adr-cdm-payload-carrier). The document itself is in the CDM payload store. The caller's key issues and accepts or rejects a proposal; the called party's key responds and proposes. Read by the collateral control contract before a pledge. Every node can read it (assumption nw-assumption-besu-visibility).

nodes.name: Oracle feed contract
nodes.description: On-chain store of the latest price / NAV, rating and default status per asset and counterparty, written only by the oracle publisher account and read by the collateral control contract.

flows.name: Initial margin call, collateral proposal and on-chain pledge
flows.description: The secured party calls initial margin and records the call on-chain; the pledgor agrees in full or in part (a disputed part is recorded but resolved off-chain) and proposes collateral; the secured party checks the proposal against its own eligibility schedule and accepts or rejects it on-chain; the pledgor pledges the accepted assets, which the collateral control contract accepts only against the agreed call and accepted proposal. Each step's CDM document goes to the CDM payload store under its keccak-256 hash and the hash goes on-chain; each party reads the other's steps from the chain and the store, verifies them and folds them into an identical MarginCallState (ADR wp-adr-cdm-payload-carrier).

transitions.description: Secured party issues an IM call under the agreement in its console.
Secured party console submits the call to the secured party's workflow service.

Secured party's service builds the issue step (CDM MarginCallInstruction, canonical Rune JSON), hashes it with keccak-256 and writes it to the payload store under that hash, with both counterparties on the reader allowlist.
Secured party's service sends the call (amount, deadline, cdmHash) to its gateway.
Secured party's gateway records the call in the margin call contract, signed with the secured party key (call state: issued; the CallIssued event carries the cdmHash).
The pledgor's gateway receives the CallIssued event from its own Besu node over its eth_subscribe subscription.
The pledgor's gateway pushes the event to the pledgor's service over Server-Sent Events; the service relays it to its console.
Pledgor's service reads the call's lifecycle steps in chain order, each with its cdmHash.
Pledgor's service fetches the issue document by its cdmHash, verifies keccak256(document) equals the on-chain hash, and folds it into its MarginCallState (Create_MarginCallState).
Pledgor responds in its console (agree, partially agree or dispute) and proposes collateral: one or more tokens and quantities.
Pledgor console submits the response and the collateral proposal to the pledgor's workflow service.
Pledgor's service fetches NAV / prices and ratings for the proposed tokens.
Pledgor's service pre-checks eligibility and haircuts against the CDM eligibility schedule and records the response and proposal in its own store.
Pledgor's service writes the response and proposal step documents to the payload store under their keccak-256 hashes.
Pledgor's service sends the response (agreed and disputed amounts) and the proposal (assets, quantities), each with its cdmHash, to its gateway.

Pledgor's gateway records the response and the proposal in the margin call contract, signed with the pledgor key (proposal state: proposed; the CallAnswered and CollateralProposed events carry the cdmHashes).

Secured party's service, notified through its gateway's event stream, reads the new steps from its gateway, fetches the response and proposal documents by cdmHash, verifies them and folds them into its MarginCallState.
Secured party's service values the proposed tokens.
Secured party's service checks eligibility, haircuts and concentration limits against its own copy of the CDM eligibility schedule and records the result.
Secured party accepts or rejects the proposal in its console; a rejection sends the pledgor back to step 10 with a new proposal.
Secured party console submits the decision to the secured party's workflow service.
Secured party's service writes the decision step document to the payload store under its keccak-256 hash.
Secured party's service sends the decision with its cdmHash to its gateway.
Secured party's gateway records the decision in the margin call contract, signed with the secured party key (proposal state: accepted; the ProposalDecided event carries the cdmHash).
Pledgor's service, notified through its gateway's event stream, fetches the decision document by cdmHash, verifies it and folds it.
Pledgor's service writes the settle step document to the payload store under its keccak-256 hash.
Pledgor's service sends a pledge instruction for every accepted asset, with the settle step's cdmHash, to its gateway.
Pledgor's gateway approves each accepted token and submits pledge(callId, proposalId, cdmHash), signed with the pledgor key.

Control contract checks the pledge against the agreed call, the accepted proposal and the agreed amount, then marks the call settled with the settle cdmHash (CallSettled); a disputed amount stays open on the call.
Contract pulls each accepted token from the pledgor's account into escrow.
Both parties' gateways receive the pledge and settlement events in finalized blocks.

Each gateway pushes the events to its own workflow service over Server-Sent Events; each service fetches, verifies and folds the settle document, and both services hold an identical MarginCallState (equal keccak stateHash).
Both consoles, updated through the services' event streams, show the settled pledge, the new balance and any disputed amount.

flows.name: Oracle price and rating update
flows.description: The oracle service publishes current NAV / price and rating data to the on-chain feed through the market operator's gateway.

transitions.description: Oracle reads mock NAV, price and rating data.
Oracle sends a signed update to the market operator's gateway.
Operator's gateway writes the update to the oracle feed contract with the oracle publisher key.

flows.name: Collateral revaluation and top-up call
flows.description: The market operator lowers the NAV or price of a pledged token; the secured party's revaluation shows a shortfall and it issues a top-up call, which then follows the IM call flow.

transitions.description: Market operator changes the NAV or price of a token.
Operator console sends the new mock value.
Oracle updates the mock market data.
Oracle publishes the new value on-chain.
Secured party's workflow service revalues pledged collateral after haircuts.
Secured party console shows the shortfall and the proposed top-up call.

flows.name: Return of initial margin
flows.description: The pledgor calls for the return of excess initial margin; the return call is recorded on-chain; the secured party agrees it through the response step and releases the escrowed tokens (issue, respond, settle). Each step is anchored by its cdmHash and its CDM document is in the CDM payload store (ADR wp-adr-cdm-payload-carrier).

transitions.description: Pledgor requests a return of excess initial margin in its console.
Pledgor console submits the request to the pledgor's workflow service.
Pledgor's service writes the return call's CDM document to the payload store under its keccak-256 hash.
Pledgor's service sends the return call (amount, cdmHash) to its gateway.
Pledgor's gateway records the return call in the margin call contract, signed with the pledgor key.
Secured party's service, notified through its gateway's event stream, fetches the return call document by cdmHash, verifies it and folds it into its MarginCallState.
Secured party agrees the return in its console.
Secured party console submits the agreement to the secured party's workflow service.
Secured party's service writes the response and settle step documents to the payload store under their keccak-256 hashes.
Secured party's service sends the response and the release instruction, each with its cdmHash, to its gateway.
Secured party's gateway records the response and submits returnCollateral(callId, assets, cdmHash), signed with the secured party key.
Control contract checks the agreed return call and amount and marks it settled with the settle cdmHash.
Contract transfers the released tokens back to the pledgor.
Each gateway pushes the Returned and CallSettled events to its own workflow service over Server-Sent Events; each service folds the settle step and updates its balance.

flows.name: Default and enforcement
flows.description: After a pledgor default, the secured party enforces against the pledged initial margin. Not wired in the prototype yet. There is no direct service-to-service channel; the pledgor learns of the default from the on-chain feed through its own gateway.

transitions.description: Secured party declares a pledgor default in its console.
Console submits the default declaration to the secured party's workflow service.
Secured party's service forwards the default notice to the oracle service.
Oracle publishes the default status through the operator's gateway.
Operator's gateway writes the default to the feed; the secured party's gateway then submits enforce() with the secured party key.
Contract confirms the default status.
Contract transfers the pledged tokens to the secured party.
Each gateway pushes the DefaultPublished and Enforced events to its own workflow service over Server-Sent Events; the pledgor's service records the default and each service records the enforcement.
